subject: using group membership as a predictor in growth()

messages.author: 9d7857a391ff2f7d
messages.subject: using group membership as a predictor in growth()
parts:
I have a series of univariate growth curve analyses to do, with models like:
 # latent intercept and slope, fixed coefficients
 i.panas_pos =~  1*panas_pos.1 + 1*panas_pos.2 + 1*panas_pos.3 + 1*panas_pos.4
 s.panas_pos =~  0*panas_pos.1 + 1*panas_pos.2 + 2*panas_pos.3 + 3*panas_pos.4
 # regressions
 i.panas_pos ~  age0 + grp
 s.panas_pos ~  age0 + grp

Normally, “grp” is an ordinary factor with two levels c("C","E"); when I run “growth(mymod,mydf)” in that case, I get a warning that grp is not ordered. If I precede growth() with
  mydf$grp<-ordered(mydf$grp)

then I get an error:
Error in samplestats@cov[[g]][cbind(row.idx, col.idx)] :
  subscript out of bounds

I tried installing the development version 5-10 but get the same message. Is there some way to do what I want to do? Have I made an error somewhere?

Thanks

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: using group membership as a predictor in growth()
parts:
On 10/18/2012 06:25 PM, Greg Shenaut wrote:
> I have a series of univariate growth curve analyses to do, with models like:
> |
> # latent intercept and slope, fixed coefficients
> i.panas_pos =~1*panas_pos.1+1*panas_pos.2+1*panas_pos.3+1*panas_pos.4
> s.panas_pos =~0*panas_pos.1+1*panas_pos.2+2*panas_pos.3+3*panas_pos.4
> # regressions
> i.panas_pos ~ age0 +grp
> s.panas_pos ~ age0 +grp
> |
>

> Normally, ï¿½grpï¿½ is an ordinary factor with two levels c("C","E"); when I
> run ï¿½growth(mymod,mydf)ï¿½ in that case, I get a warning that grp is not
> ordered.

Indeed. This is a reminder that lavaan syntax (unlike, say, lm formulas)
does (currently) NOT automatically expand nominal factors to a set of
dummy variables. You should take care of that yourself. If you have two
levels, you just need a (numeric) binary variable with two values (say 1
and 0). As long as it is an exogenous (independent) variable, there is
no need to treat it special.

If I precede growth() with

> mydf$grp<-ordered(mydf$grp)
> |
>
> then I get an error:
> |
> Errorinsamplestats@cov[[g]][cbind(row.idx,col.idx)]:
> subscript outof bounds

That is because lavaan can not handle 'ordered' exogenous variables (and
your group variable is not ordered; it is just nominal). On the other
hand, lavaan could catch this, convert it back to numeric, and proceed
as usual. I'll fix this in the dev version. (But in the meantime, do not
'order' exogenous variables).

Yves.
